title: Using MetaboAnalyst 6.0 for Exposomics Data Analysis
author: Zhiqiang Pang
materials: Unzip the dataset #1 (NP_exposome_raw.zip) into individual files.

steps.title: Initialize Spectra Processing Module
steps.instruction: Visit the MetaboAnalyst home page (https://www.metaboanalyst.ca/), click 'Click here to start' to reach the 'Module Overview' page, and select 'Spectra Processing [LC-MS w/wo MS2]'.

steps.title: Upload Spectral Data
steps.instruction: Upload the raw spectral files and metadata.

substeps.instruction: Optionally, select the 'E-Waste dataset' from example datasets to skip to Step 7.
Click 'Select' and upload all 19 *.zip files along with the sample.txt metadata file.
Click 'Upload' to start the process.
If using the complete dataset (109 samples), repeat the upload process for all files.
Ensure 'Select Mode' is set to 'MS1+DDA' and click 'Proceed'.

steps.title: Perform Data Integrity Check
steps.instruction: Review the uploaded spectra in the summary table (columns: Spectra, Centroid, Size (MB), MS Level, Group).

substeps.instruction: Use the 'Include' column checkboxes to include or exclude specific spectra.
Verify the 'Centroid' column; spectra flagged as 'False' are automatically excluded unless fixed via the 'Convert' button.
Click 'Next'.

steps.title: Customize LC-MS/MS Processing Parameters
steps.instruction: Navigate to the 'LC-MS/MS Spectra Processing' page and configure the pipeline.

substeps.instruction: Set the platform to 'UPLC-Q/E' to load default parameters.
Select 'MS1+SWATH-DIA' if MS2 spectra were acquired in SWATH-DIA mode.
Change the peak detection algorithm from 'centWave-auto' to 'Asari' for higher sensitivity to trace-level features.
Manually adjust peak alignment and annotation parameters if required for the specific dataset (keep default for e-waste dataset).
Set MS2 processing parameters: 'Target Peaks' to 'All Features', 'MS2 Database' to 'All Database', and 'Target Omics' to 'Exposomics'.
Keep all other parameters as default.

steps.title: Submit and Monitor Job
steps.instruction: Submit the raw spectra for processing and track the status.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Submit Job' and then 'Confirm'.
On the 'Job Status View' page, click 'Create Job URL' and 'Copy' to save the unique link for later access.
Monitor the progress bar until it reaches 100% and the success message appears.
Click 'Proceed' upon completion.

steps.title: Explore LC-MS Results
steps.instruction: Analyze the generated graphical summaries and tabular outputs.

substeps.instruction: Use the Interactive 3D PCA visualization to explore MS features; switch between scores plot (main) and loadings plot (inset) using the double arrow icon.
Double-click data points in the PCA loading plot to view intensity distribution box plots and extracted ion chromatograms (EIC).
Review the intensity plot, TIC (total ion chromatogram), and BPI (base peak ion) plots.
Examine the sample/spectra table and the feature/peak table (containing m/z, RT, intensity, CV, p-values, FDR, and adducts).
Check the MS2 results table for compound annotations, expanding rows to view matching scores and mirror plots.
Use the 'MS2 only' checkbox on the PCA loading plot to highlight features with MS2 metadata.

steps.title: Download Stage 1 Results
steps.instruction: Click the 'Download' link to retrieve the following files: metaboanalyst_input.csv, metaboanalyst_input_compounds.csv, metaboanalyst_input_clean.csv, Compound_msn_results.csv, and metaboanalyst_feature_reference.csv.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Enter the 'Statistical Analysis [metadata table]' module from the home page.

substeps.instruction: Set data type to 'Peak intensities', study design to 'Multiple factors / covariates', and data format to 'Samples in columns'.
Upload the data file (e.g., ewaste_data_QC.csv) and metadata file (e.g., ewaste_metadata.csv) and click 'Submit'.
Review the data and metadata integrity check pages and click 'Proceed'.
Apply 'low-quality filter' with 'Enable missing-value exclusion' set to 50% (or 'Group-wise threshold').
Apply 'low-repeatability filter' with QC RSD cutoff at 20%.
Set low-variance and low-abundance filters to 0% using the sliders.
Click 'Submit' and then 'Proceed'.

steps.title: Impute Missing Values and Normalize Data
steps.instruction: Address missing data and normalize intensities to reduce heterogeneity.

substeps.instruction: Under 'Left-censored data estimation', select 'quantile regression (QRILC)' and click 'Submit', then 'Proceed'.
Select 'Normalization by median' under 'Sample Normalization'.
Select 'Variance stabilizing normalization' (VSN) under 'Data Transformation' and click 'Normalize'.
Click 'View Result' to compare density plots and boxplots before and after normalization, then click 'Proceed'.

steps.title: Remove QC Samples
steps.instruction: Exclude QC samples to ensure downstream biological analysis is not biased.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Interactive PCA Visualization' to verify QC clustering.
Go to 'Data Editor', search for 'QC', select QC samples 1 to 6, and move them to the exclusion list.
Click 'Submit'.
Re-apply 'Normalization by median' and 'Variance stabilizing normalization' and click 'Normalize'.

steps.title: Perform Exploratory Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Use PCA and metadata visualization to identify patterns.

substeps.instruction: Click 'iPCA' to view the PCA plot and PERMANOVA p-values.
Use 'Synchronized PCA 3D' and apply confidence ellipsoids via the ellipse icon.
Use 'Metadata Visualization' to generate a hierarchical clustering heatmap.
Use the 'Correlation Heatmap' tab; switch to 'Pearson (partial)' and click 'Update' to uncover direct relationships between metadata factors.

steps.title: Execute Linear Modeling with Covariates
steps.instruction: Identify features associated with the primary exposure while adjusting for confounders.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Linear Model' and select the primary metadata (e.g., 'BCd').
Select 'Raw' for the P-value cutoff and click 'Submit'.
Analyze the scatter plot of unadjusted vs. adjusted p-values.
Double-click features to view violin or regression plots.
Download the result table ('covariate_result.csv').

steps.title: Perform Functional Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the biological pathways of the significant features.

substeps.instruction: Edit 'covariate_result.csv' to keep only feature names, raw p-values, and t-scores; rename columns to 'm.z', 'p.value', and 't.score'.
Upload this file to the 'Functional Analysis [LC-MS]' module using the 'A peak list profile' tab.
Set 'Retention time' to 'Yes - Seconds' and use default parameters for processing.
On the 'Mummichog Pathway Activity Profile' page, select 'Enrichment Network'.
Adjust the 'Overlap threshold' in the 'Edge' menu and use 'Bipartite View' to expand pathway nodes.

steps.title: Visualize Results via Heatmap
steps.instruction: Generate an interactive heatmap for high-dimensional data visualization.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Heatmap2' in the navigation tree.
Update 'Metadata in annotation' to include relevant covariates (e.g., BCd, Age, BMI, Smoking, Alcohol).
Set 'Sample arrangement' to the primary exposure (e.g., 'BCd') and click 'Submit'.

steps.title: Perform Random Forest Analysis
steps.instruction: Use Random Forest for classification or regression of the exposure variable.

substeps.instruction: For classification: Select 'BCd_group' as the outcome, optionally add predictors (e.g., 'Age'), and click 'Update'.
For regression: Set 'Primary metadata' to 'BCd' and click 'Update'.
Review the OOB error/MSE and the 'Var. Importance' dot plot to identify top-ranked features.

steps.title: Conduct Dose Response Analysis
steps.instruction: Model the relationship between feature abundance and continuous exposure.

substeps.instruction: Enter the 'Dose Response Analysis' module and upload the feature abundance table and metadata table.
Set data type to 'Peak intensities' and dose type to 'Continuous Dosing'.
Normalize using 'Normalization by median' and 'Variance stabilizing normalization'.
Perform feature selection: add covariates (e.g., Age, BMI, Alcohol, Smoking), uncheck 'Adjusted p-value (FDR)', set regression coefficient to 0.0, and click 'Submit'.
Proceed to 'Curve fitting' using default models (avoid selecting more than 5 models to save time) and click 'Submit'.
Review the BMD (Benchmark Dose) distribution and individual fitted curves via the 'View' button.
Cross-reference results with 'compound_msn_results.csv' from Stage 1.

steps.title: Perform Causal Analysis (Mendelian Randomization)
steps.instruction: Estimate causal relationships between metabolites and outcomes using genetic instruments.

substeps.instruction: Enter the 'Causal Analysis [Mendelian randomization]' module.
Select an exposure (e.g., 'L-isoleucine') and an outcome (e.g., 'type 2 diabetes' -> 'finn-b-E4_DM2').
Filter and harmonize SNPs: perform LD clumping, disable proxy variants, harmonize alleles by frequency, and apply Steiger filtering. Click 'Submit'.
Select MR methods (e.g., IVW-FE, IVW-MRE, Weighted Median, Simple Mode, Weighted Mode, and MR-Egger) and click 'Proceed'.
Analyze the MR result table and graphical outputs (Forest plot, Scatter plot, and Funnel plot).
Explore 'Literature Evidence' and 'Variant Effect (AlphaGenome)' tabs for mechanistic insights.

description: Explore the summary pie charts for metabolome and exposome ( Figure 2B ). The metabolome pie chart summarizes chemical taxonomies of all identified compounds based on the HMDB classification 42 . The exposome pie chart summarizes all annotated exposome-related compounds based on the categories from NORMAN Suspect List Exchange database 43 . More details will be discussed on Step 29.
